original_response.display: “Borrowed a folder? Give it back to the conductor” gives a new singer a clear action. For the other path, use the lesson’s test: can the singer tell what to do from the note alone? If someone owns a folder but left it in the choir room last week, what would “If you brought your own, keep it” lead them to do? If they might hesitate, try one small edit in your own words that makes ownership the deciding detail.

packet.submission:
Borrowed a folder? Give it back to the conductor. If you brought your own, keep it.

I used “borrowed” and “your own” so a new singer can tell which instruction applies. I went with “brought your own,” but I wonder if that sounds like it only applies to folders brought from home.

packet.evidence_limit: Review covers the submitted passage and its editing rationale. Several voices and arrangements can serve the same reader. Whether real readers understood it needs a reader observation. Fiction, poetry, the learner's overall talent and any private writing remain outside this finding.

packet.learner: I'd like to get back to working on my writing. You can use the broad goal and the kind of exercise I said you could keep. Can you give me feedback on this choir note?

material.excerpt: A new reader may see two possible actions. Look for the detail that tells them which applies. Trace each path through the draft before deciding whether the wording will do.
material.lesson: For a passage with two possible actions, imagine the reader encountering each situation separately. Read only what you have put on the page. See whether either reader has to supply a missing rule.

packet.policy: Honor stop immediately. At a return without shared work, follow the current request. Ask one focused question if needed, otherwise defer. Resume only in a separate learner-initiated meeting with fresh sharing and release permission. Use the new prompt and submission. Honor an explicit skip or change of target. If a permitted phrase and applicable reviewed lesson criterion are available, quote the phrase, name the criterion, and ask what the wording would lead a reader to infer or do. Invite one small edit of the writer's choosing if that reading misses the task or admits a competing reading. If the lesson is unavailable or inapplicable, use the exact-phrase probe with the task and any available excerpt. If no permitted target remains, set the exercise aside. Confirm a booking only when the application confirms it.
